summary: Backend-only retest after MoMo /public/payments/transfer payload restructure. ALL 16 pytest tests PASS (16/16 = 100%). CORE FIX VERIFIED: BeSoft no longer returns 'Invalid request body — Key: TransferRequest.Debit.Amount required'. Backend logs at 11:57:15+ show POST /public/payments/transfer returning HTTP 201 Created (previously HTTP 400 with the flat payload). The payload is now correctly nested as { idempotency_key, debit: { amount, currency, payment_method, payer_identifier, description, country, metadata } } per BeSoft openapi.yaml TransferRequest schema. Verified in server.py:833-844 (subscription) and server.py:1454-1465 (VOD). Payment docs now correctly persist besoftAttempt='transfer_collection' on both success and failure branches (previous iteration bug fixed at server.py:1493 in the VOD failure branch). Safety guard (merchant number 250798875274) still blocks all 3 normalization variants in both subscription and VOD paths (HTTP 400 'collection account'). PayPal regressions all pass: /billing/paypal/create-subscription returns subscriptionId + paypal.com approveUrl; /billing/vod/{id}/create returns orderId + paypal.com approveUrl. Health = 200, guest /api/shows returns list, /api/shows/{id} without auth returns locked=true. MINOR RESIDUAL BEHAVIOR: The /debit-credit legacy fallback in server.py:873-903 is STILL being invoked after /transfer, but ONLY because the inner debit_norm comes back as 'failed' with 'provider error [HTTP_400]' (MTN-side error on the test payer, not a BeSoft validation error). Because the fallback call also returns failed, besoftAttempt correctly stays as 'transfer_collection' (server.py:900 check). The /transfer HTTP layer itself is healthy (201). This is per the review spec's ACCEPTABLE criteria ('failed with an MTN-side reason' is fine — we only need to prove the payload is accepted at BeSoft's validation layer, which it is).

minor.issue: Legacy /debit-credit fallback (server.py:873-903) still fires whenever the inner debit.status == 'failed' with any HTTP_400 marker inside the failure_reason string — even when the outer /transfer HTTP response is now healthy 201 Created. Suggest tightening the guard so fallback only triggers on outer HTTP >= 300 (not on MTN-side per-transaction failures like insufficient balance). besoftAttempt is preserved as 'transfer_collection' because the fallback also fails, but this wastes an extra HTTP call and keeps the deprecated endpoint alive. Review-request note explicitly said fallback 'should NOT be triggered anymore on a healthy /transfer response'.

action_items: OPTIONAL — Tighten the fallback trigger in /billing/momo/initiate (server.py:873-877): change `should_fallback = (status_code >= 300 or debit_norm == 'failed')` to just `should_fallback = status_code >= 300`, so MTN-side per-transaction failures (insufficient balance, not registered, HTTP_400 inside a 201 envelope) do not trigger an extra legacy /debit-credit hit. Right now /debit-credit is called on every failed test payer transaction even though /transfer returned 201.
OPTIONAL — Remove the /debit-credit legacy fallback entirely (server.py:878-903) once the above is verified in production. The core payload migration is done and validated at BeSoft's schema layer.

rca_of_issue: The critical bug from iteration 17 (BeSoft HTTP 400 'Invalid request body — Key: TransferRequest.Debit.Amount required') is RESOLVED. Root cause was a flat payload shape that did not match BeSoft's openapi.yaml TransferRequest schema (nested {idempotency_key, debit:{...}}). Fix applied in server.py:833-844 (subscription) and server.py:1454-1465 (VOD). Backend logs confirm the /transfer endpoint now returns HTTP 201 Created (log lines at 11:57:15, 11:57:18, 11:57:22 UTC). Payment docs written after the fix persist besoftAttempt='transfer_collection' as expected (verified via db.payments and db.vod_purchases queries). The only remaining observation is a stale fallback branch that fires on MTN-side transaction failures even though the /transfer wrapper is now healthy — cosmetic/perf issue, not a correctness issue.
